# ShopMind repository-wide conventions

- Use Python 3.12 and uv for dependencies and commands. Respect `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`; check existing versions before adding or changing dependencies.
- Read nearby code and tests first. Follow existing naming, typing, dependency injection, error handling and project structure. Make focused changes for the requested increment; avoid unrelated fixes, refactors and infrastructure.
- Follow the detailed module instructions in [API](instructions/shopmind-api.instructions.md), [AI](instructions/shopmind-ai.instructions.md) and [MCP](instructions/shopmind-mcp.instructions.md). Treat roadmap descriptions and historical test results as plans/reports, not verified current behavior.
- Keep module boundaries: `shopmind_api` owns commerce rules, identity, authorization, data integrity and transactions; `shopmind_ai` owns AI workflows and retrieval, including its own AI-specific PostgreSQL/pgvector data; `shopmind_mcp` owns protocol and integration adapters. AI and MCP obtain commerce data through approved API interfaces, never direct commerce-table access.
- PostgreSQL is the persistent source of truth (PostgreSQL 17 in the current Compose setup). Use Alembic for schema changes; add migrations rather than rewriting applied migrations. Make transaction, rollback and retry behavior explicit. Do not apply migrations to a shared database without confirming the intended environment.
- Keep environment-specific configuration and secrets outside source control. Never commit or log `.env` contents, credentials, JWTs, passwords or payment data; never send them to model prompts. Preserve verified identity, backend authorization and ownership checks. Do not weaken validation or silently substitute privileged credentials.
- Use pytest for automated tests and Ruff for linting/formatting, via `uv run`. Run focused checks for affected behavior first and expand when needed. Add deterministic tests for changed contracts, validation, failure paths and relevant authorization/transaction boundaries; do not require live providers or production credentials for unit tests.
- Update directly related documentation when behavior or setup changes. Report only checks actually run and distinguish verified outcomes from assumptions. Preserve unrelated worktree changes.
